body:
Found by cross-model review of PR #502 (T-01KZY120SZP96QKEEXDKZEZJR5), where it was measured and ruled out as that branch's defect: it predates the branch and lives here.

`globMatch` (packages/core/lib/tickets.mjs) compiles a rail glob to a regular expression. On a rail with repeated `**` segments the expression backtracks catastrophically against a path that ALMOST matches, and every rail-enforcement path in the repo calls it before anything else.

=== MEASURED ===

On merged main (e87c933d), node 22:

  globMatch('a/' + '**/'.repeat(15) + 'z', <17-segment path>)   -> false, 5669 ms
  globMatch('a/' + '**/'.repeat(12) + 'z', <22-segment path>)   -> false, 6470 ms
  globMatch('a/' + '**/'.repeat(8)  + 'z', <32-segment path>)   -> false,  973 ms
  globMatch('a/' + '**/'.repeat(200)+ 'z', <16001-segment path>) -> did not finish in 10 minutes

For comparison, the opencode ancestor walk on that last input returns in 1029 ms, which is why capping the walk does not address this: the matcher that runs first dominates by orders of magnitude.

=== REACHABILITY, AND WHY THIS IS NOT URGENT ===

The rail string comes from the ticket store, which is a trust root. A caller who can author `a/**/**/.../z` can equally delete the rail set, so this is not a privilege boundary being crossed. What it is: a repository whose own ticket data can wedge a synchronous pre-execution hook in every adapter, with no error and no decision, until the ticket is repaired. That is a robustness defect in a component all four adapters depend on, and it is invisible until someone writes an unusual rail.

The path length is caller-controlled, but the globstar count is not, and both are needed for the blowup.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `globMatch` answers a repeated-globstar rail against a long non-matching path in bounded time -- the four measurements above complete in well under a second each. verify: `node --test packages/core/test/core.test.mjs`
- The answers do not change: existing glob semantics are pinned by the current suite, including `**` spanning `/` inside a segment (`a/foo**bar/**` matches `a/foo/x/bar/frozen.mjs`). verify: `node --test packages/core/test/*.test.mjs`
- A regression test uses an input that does not finish today, so the fix is proven rather than asserted. verify: `node --test packages/core/test/core.test.mjs`
- The three CI gates pass on a freshly fetched base. verify: `npm run preflight`

allow-suppression: none

=== NOTES FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS ===

A linear matcher over segments (the two-transition shape `plugins/adlc-opencode/rails-checker.mjs` uses for ancestry after PR #502) is one option, but it must reproduce the embedded-`**` semantics exactly -- that spelling is load-bearing and is what makes the current expression span `/`. Pinning the current behaviour before changing the engine is the cheap first step.

Rejecting pathological rails at load time is the other option and is smaller, but it moves a runtime hazard into a validation rule that every store writer then has to satisfy.
title: core: globMatch backtracks catastrophically on a repeated-globstar rail
